title: Transcriptomics and OsWAK24–MPK3 crosstalk reveal resistance mechanism of primed rice seedlings against arsenic–iron
content:
Abstract
Priming (a form of memory) refers to the pre-conditioning of plant stress responses to enhance resilience towards future stressors, including arsenic (As) contamination. This adaptive preparedness becomes more complex under As–Fe (iron) interplay, which has not been delineated in a priming background. Here, we employed Illumina sequencing to acquire global transcriptome alterations, and a heterologous interaction approach to chart the molecular reprogramming associated with As and As–Fe dynamics in primed rice. The transcriptome revealed that 3005 and 3650 genes are differentially regulated in As- and As–Fe-exposed primed seedlings. Comprehensive expression profiling revealed that key genes were involved in transportation (OsNramp, OsFCR, and OsNAS), signalling (OsWRKY, OsMYB, OsAP2, and OsZF-TF), and defence (OsHSP, OsPRX, and OsCyt P450). Expression of antioxidant genes (OsGST and OsAPX) correlated well with their respective physiological enzyme activity. The entire wall-associated kinase (WAK) module, transducing extracellular signals to intercellular pathways, was differentially regulated under the influence of As and As–Fe. Notably, OsWAK24 revealed higher expression under As–Fe, reflecting its association with the tolerance behaviour of seedlings. The computational protein network and docking revealed OsMPK3 as an interactor of OsWAK24. Split-ubiquitin-based yeast hybrid assay and immunoblot revealed OsWAK24–OsMPK3 association, suggesting that phosphorylation mediated interaction of OsWAK24 and OsMPK3 at a serine residue. Overall, the results decoded the resilience mechanism of seedlings and will aid in developing rice varieties with desired traits.
